I located the likely faults but did not change project source or tests; this run is restricted to fault localization.

In [module_common.py](/app/lib/ansible/executor/module_common.py:657), collection lookup does not read `plugin_routing.module_utils`, so redirects and their targets are omitted. In [recursive_finder](/app/lib/ansible/executor/module_common.py:720), collection package initializers are packaged under the wrong name while ancestor initializers are replaced with empty files. That also prevents their relative imports from being discovered. The same resolver tries only the last one or two import components and reports leaf names rather than all attempted paths.

The fix should use queued dependency work and separate legacy and collection locators, preserve real package `__init__.py` source, synthesize missing package levels, and process redirect shims and metadata with full candidate paths in errors. The existing `recursive_finder` unit suite passes (8 tests), but it does not cover these collection cases. Detailed findings and remaining uncertainty are in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md).

Updated [module_common.py](/app/lib/ansible/executor/module_common.py) to resolve `module_utils` dependencies through a queue and separate legacy and collection locators. The payload now includes redirect shims, real package initializer source, and empty initializers for missing parent packages. Unresolved import errors list the attempted paths.

Added focused coverage in [test_recursive_finder.py](/app/test/units/executor/module_common/test_recursive_finder.py). The local `module_common` suite passes: **49 tests**. `git diff --check` is clean.

VERDICT: FIX

The patch has two correctness defects:

- [module_common.py](/app/lib/ansible/executor/module_common.py:745) rejects nested legacy redirect names. The repository metadata includes `sub1.sub2.formerly_core`, but a local locator probe returned `found=False`. The locator needs to look up the full dotted name after `ansible.module_utils`.
- [module_common.py](/app/lib/ansible/executor/module_common.py:756) raises a raw `ModuleNotFoundError` when a redirect targets a missing collection. A local probe confirmed the error lacks the required `unable to locate collection <fqcn>` message. Convert that failure to the required `AnsibleError`.

**Tests:** `PYTHONPATH=lib python -m pytest -q test/units/executor/module_common/test_recursive_finder.py test/units/executor/module_common/test_module_common.py test/units/executor/module_common/test_modify_module.py` — 49 passed. No test environment problem.

Fixed both reviewed defects in [module_common.py](/app/lib/ansible/executor/module_common.py): legacy redirects now use the full dotted name below `ansible.module_utils`, and a missing redirect target collection raises an `AnsibleError` naming that collection. Added regression tests.

The exact test command from the review passed: **51 passed**. `git diff --check` also passed.
